"""The Lux-Marchesi (1999) market model, built from the equations in notes/SPEC.md.

N traders are in one of three groups:
    fundamentalists  buy when the price is below the fundamental value, sell above it
    optimists        chartists who buy
    pessimists       chartists who sell
Traders switch groups at random, at rates that depend on the crowd (herding), the
price trend and the profits of each strategy. Excess demand (buyers minus sellers)
moves the price one tick at a time. News moves the fundamental value as Gaussian
noise, so any fat tails or volatility clustering must come from the traders.

Section numbers (sec. 1-5) refer to notes/SPEC.md.

Policy options (an extension, not part of the paper; SPEC.md "Policy experiments"):
circuit breakers that pause or close trading after a big fall within the day, and
one-off policy surprises that move the fundamental value.
"""
import os

import numpy as np

try:
    import numba
except ImportError:                    # still works without numba, just ~50x slower
    numba = None

# Settings. Every one has a fixed meaning in SPEC.md; rates are per unit of time
# (one unit = one trading day).
SETTINGS = {
    "N": "number of traders",
    "v1": "how often chartists reconsider their mood (sec. 1)",
    "v2": "how often traders reconsider their strategy (sec. 2)",
    "a1": "herding: weight of the majority mood (sec. 1)",
    "a2": "trend following: weight of the price trend (sec. 1)",
    "a3": "sensitivity to profit differences (sec. 2)",
    "s": "discount on fundamentalists' future profits, below 1 (sec. 2)",
    "R": "return on other investments per day; dividend yield r/p_f = R (sec. 2)",
    "tc": "trading volume of one chartist (sec. 3)",
    "gamma": "reaction strength of one fundamentalist (sec. 3)",
    "beta": "price speed: relative price change per day per unit of excess demand (sec. 3)",
    "sigma_mu": "standard deviation of the noise in excess demand (sec. 3)",
    "sigma_eps": "daily standard deviation of the news (sec. 4)",
    "tick": "size of one price tick, as a fraction of the price (sec. 3)",
    "dt": "time step, as a fraction of a day (sec. 5)",
    "floor": "minimum number of chartists and of fundamentalists (sec. 5)",
}

# Parameter set I as remembered from Lux & Marchesi (2000), UNVERIFIED (SPEC.md).
# T_c = N tc = 10 and T_f = N gamma = 5.
SET_I = dict(N=500, v1=3.0, v2=2.0, a1=0.6, a2=0.2, a3=0.5, s=0.75, R=0.0004,
             tc=0.02, gamma=0.01, beta=6.0, sigma_mu=0.05, sigma_eps=0.005,
             tick=0.001, dt=0.01, floor=4)

TREND_WINDOW = 0.1     # dp/dt is measured over the last 0.1 day (= 10 steps of 0.01) [S]
REFERENCE_DT = 0.01    # the time step of Lux & Marchesi's own simulations [S]
U_CAP = 30.0           # cap on the exponents U, so exp(U) cannot overflow
MAX_GAP = 1.0          # a runaway: the price more than e = 2.7x away from its value...
MAX_DAYS = 250         # ...for a whole year of trading days in a row,
HARD_GAP = 20.0        # or ever more than e^20 (5 hundred million) times away
START_CHARTISTS = 0.1  # share of chartists at the start, split evenly into the two moods
# US market-wide circuit breakers since 2013 (NYSE Rule 7.12, formerly Rule 80B;
# SEC-approved): a 15-minute pause when the S&P 500 is 7% or 13% below the previous
# close, but only before 3:25 pm (minute 355 of the day); closed for the day at 20%
# at any time.
US_BREAKERS = dict(levels=(0.07, 0.13, 0.20), halt_minutes=15, last_pause_minute=355)
MINUTES_PER_DAY = 390  # 9:30 to 16:00


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ checks

class RunawayError(RuntimeError):
    """The price left its value for good (all traders became chartists)."""

    def __init__(self, message, day):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.day = day


def check(p):
    """Raise ValueError unless p has exactly the known settings with sensible values."""
    if not isinstance(p, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"settings must be a dict, got {type(p).__name__}")
    unknown, missing = set(p) - set(SETTINGS), set(SETTINGS) - set(p)
    if unknown or missing:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown settings {sorted(unknown)}, missing settings {sorted(missing)}")
    for k, v in p.items():
        if isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(v, (int, float, np.number)) \
                or not np.isfinite(v):
            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be a finite number, got {v!r}")
        if v < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must not be negative, got {v}")
    # floor 0 would let the chartists die out: then opinion x = (n+ - n-)/n_c divides by 0
    for k in ("N", "v1", "v2", "beta", "tick", "dt", "floor"):
        if p[k] <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be above 0, got {p[k]}")
    for k in ("N", "floor"):
        if int(p[k]) != p[k]:
            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be a whole number, got {p[k]}")
    if not p["s"] < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"s must be below 1 (the paper's discount factor), got {p['s']}")
    if not p["tick"] < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"tick must be below 1 (a fraction of the price), got {p['tick']}")
    steps = round(1 / p["dt"])
    if abs(steps * p["dt"] - 1) > 1e-9:
        raise ValueError(f"dt must split one day into whole steps (0.01, 0.005, ...), got {p['dt']}")
    if TREND_WINDOW / p["dt"] < 1 - 1e-9:
        raise ValueError(f"dt must be at most {TREND_WINDOW} (the trend window), got {p['dt']}")
    if p["N"] < 4 * p["floor"]:
        raise ValueError(f"N={p['N']} is too small for floor={p['floor']}: need N >= 4*floor")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ one time step

def _leave(g, n, rate_a, rate_b, dt):
    """Of n traders each leaving at rate_a (to A) or rate_b (to B) per day, how many
    go to A and to B within dt. Exact for constant rates: a trader leaves with
    probability 1 - exp(-(rate_a + rate_b) dt), then picks A with chance
    rate_a / (rate_a + rate_b)."""
    total = rate_a + rate_b
    if n <= 0 or total <= 0.0:
        return 0, 0
    k = g.binomial(n, 1.0 - np.exp(-total * dt))
    to_a = g.binomial(k, rate_a / total)
    return to_a, k - to_a


def _cap(u):
    return min(U_CAP, max(-U_CAP, u))


def _simulate(g, days, steps, chartists, N, v1, v2, a1, a2, a3, s, R, tc, gamma,
              beta, sigma_mu, sigma_eps, tick, floor, n_plus, n_minus, max_gap, max_days,
              hard_gap, cb1, cb2, cb3, halt_steps, pause_end, shock):
    """The simulation loop (see SPEC.md). Returns per-day log price, log value,
    chartist share and opinion at each day's close, the circuit-breaker level of
    each day, and the number of days completed (fewer than `days` if the price ran
    away: |log price - log value| above max_gap for max_days days in a row, or ever
    above hard_gap).
    Circuit breakers: 0 > cb1 > cb2 > cb3 are log falls from the previous close
    (-inf = off). Falling to cb1 or cb2 within the first pause_end steps of the day
    freezes the price for halt_steps steps (once each per day; later in the day
    nothing happens); falling to cb3 freezes it for the rest of the day, at any time.
    Traders keep switching while the price is frozen.
    shock[day]: log change of the value at the start of that day (policy surprise)."""
    dt = 1.0 / steps
    window = int(round(TREND_WINDOW * steps))
    up_step, down_step = np.log(1.0 + tick), np.log(1.0 - tick)
    # mu is drawn fresh each step; scaled so its effect per day does not depend on
    # dt (identical to [S] at their dt = 0.01)
    mu_sd = sigma_mu * np.sqrt(REFERENCE_DT / dt)
    lp = 0.0                                   # log price; starts at the value
    lf = 0.0                                   # log fundamental value
    n_f = N - n_plus - n_minus
    past = np.zeros(window)                    # log prices of the last `window` steps
    out_lp = np.empty(days + 1)
    out_lf = np.empty(days + 1)
    out_z = np.empty(days + 1)
    out_x = np.empty(days + 1)
    out_lp[0], out_lf[0] = lp, lf
    nc = n_plus + n_minus
    out_z[0] = nc / N
    out_x[0] = (n_plus - n_minus) / nc if nc > 0 else 0.0
    halts = np.zeros(days, dtype=np.int64)     # 0 none, 1-2 pause levels, 3 closed
    t = 0
    outside = 0                                # days in a row beyond max_gap
    for day in range(days):
        lf += shock[day]
        prev_close = lp
        paused = 0                             # steps of pause left
        for k in range(steps):
            # dp/dt / p: relative price change per day over the trend window
            trend = (np.exp(lp - past[t % window]) - 1.0) / TREND_WINDOW
            past[t % window] = lp
            t += 1
            gap = np.exp(lf - lp) - 1.0        # (p_f - p) / p
            if chartists:
                nc = n_plus + n_minus
                # sec. 1: mood. sec. 2: strategy (profit of chartists vs fundamentalists)
                U1 = _cap(a1 * (n_plus - n_minus) / nc + a2 / v1 * trend)
                gain = R * (1.0 + gap) + trend / v2    # (r + (dp/dt)/v2) / p, r = R p_f
                U21 = _cap(a3 * (gain - R - s * abs(gap)))
                U22 = _cap(a3 * (R - gain - s * abs(gap)))
                mood = v1 * nc / N
                # every rate below is per trader per day (first: where they go)
                p_to_m, p_to_f = _leave(g, n_plus, mood * np.exp(-U1),
                                        v2 * n_f / N * np.exp(-U21), dt)
                m_to_p, m_to_f = _leave(g, n_minus, mood * np.exp(U1),
                                        v2 * n_f / N * np.exp(-U22), dt)
                f_to_p, f_to_m = _leave(g, n_f, v2 * n_plus / N * np.exp(U21),
                                        v2 * n_minus / N * np.exp(U22), dt)
                # floors (sec. 5): undo just enough moves to keep both groups alive
                short_f = floor - (n_f - f_to_p - f_to_m + p_to_f + m_to_f)
                while short_f > 0:
                    if f_to_p >= f_to_m:
                        f_to_p -= 1
                    else:
                        f_to_m -= 1
                    short_f -= 1
                short_c = floor - (nc - p_to_f - m_to_f + f_to_p + f_to_m)
                while short_c > 0:
                    if p_to_f >= m_to_f:
                        p_to_f -= 1
                    else:
                        m_to_f -= 1
                    short_c -= 1
                n_plus += m_to_p - p_to_m + f_to_p - p_to_f
                n_minus += p_to_m - m_to_p + f_to_m - m_to_f
                n_f += p_to_f + m_to_f - f_to_p - f_to_m
            # sec. 3: excess demand -> random up and down ticks
            ed = (n_plus - n_minus) * tc + n_f * gamma * gap
            # ticks per day = beta (ED + mu) / tick, so that on average
            # d(ln p)/dt = beta (ED + mu), SPEC eq. 25
            push = beta * (ed + mu_sd * g.standard_normal()) / tick
            if halts[day] == 3 or paused > 0:  # trading halted: the price is frozen
                paused = max(0, paused - 1)
            else:
                if push > 0.0:
                    lp += g.poisson(push * dt) * up_step
                else:
                    lp += g.poisson(-push * dt) * down_step
                # circuit breakers: each level fires at most once a day
                fall = lp - prev_close
                if fall <= cb3:
                    halts[day] = 3
                elif fall <= cb2 and halts[day] < 2 and k < pause_end:
                    halts[day] = 2
                    paused = halt_steps
                elif fall <= cb1 and halts[day] < 1 and k < pause_end:
                    halts[day] = 1
                    paused = halt_steps
            # sec. 4: news
            lf += sigma_eps * np.sqrt(dt) * g.standard_normal()
        nc = n_plus + n_minus
        out_lp[day + 1], out_lf[day + 1] = lp, lf
        out_z[day + 1] = nc / N
        out_x[day + 1] = (n_plus - n_minus) / nc if nc > 0 else 0.0
        outside = outside + 1 if abs(lp - lf) > max_gap else 0
        if outside >= max_days or abs(lp - lf) > hard_gap:
            return out_lp, out_lf, out_z, out_x, halts, day + 1
    return out_lp, out_lf, out_z, out_x, halts, days


USE_NUMBA = numba is not None and os.environ.get("MODEL_NO_NUMBA") != "1"
if USE_NUMBA:
    _leave = numba.njit(cache=True)(_leave)
    _cap = numba.njit(cache=True)(_cap)
    _simulate = numba.njit(cache=True)(_simulate)


def check_breakers(breakers):
    """Circuit-breaker rules: dict(levels=(l1, l2, l3), halt_minutes=m), and optionally
    last_pause_minute=c. The levels are falls below the previous close (0.07 = 7%),
    increasing; l1 and l2 pause trading for m minutes of a 390-minute day, but only
    before minute c (no limit if c is left out); l3 closes the day at any time.
    None = no breakers."""
    if breakers is None:
        return
    if not isinstance(breakers, dict) or not {"levels", "halt_minutes"} <= set(breakers) \
            or not set(breakers) <= {"levels", "halt_minutes", "last_pause_minute"}:
        raise ValueError("breakers needs 'levels' and 'halt_minutes' (and optionally "
                         f"'last_pause_minute'), got {breakers!r}")
    c = breakers.get("last_pause_minute", MINUTES_PER_DAY)
    if not _is_number(c) or not 0 <= c <= MINUTES_PER_DAY:
        raise ValueError(f"last_pause_minute must be a number from 0 to {MINUTES_PER_DAY}, got {c!r}")
    lv = tuple(breakers["levels"])
    if len(lv) != 3 or not all(_is_number(x) and 0 < x < 1 for x in lv) \
            or not lv[0] < lv[1] < lv[2]:
        raise ValueError(f"breaker levels must be 3 increasing falls between 0 and 1, got {lv}")
    m = breakers["halt_minutes"]
    if not _is_number(m) or not 0 < m <= MINUTES_PER_DAY:
        raise ValueError(f"halt_minutes must be a number from 0 to {MINUTES_PER_DAY}, got {m!r}")


def check_shocks(shocks, days):
    """Policy surprises: {day: fraction}, e.g. {200: -0.1} = at the start of day 200
    a surprise cuts the fundamental value by 10%. None = no surprises."""
    if shocks is None:
        return
    if not isinstance(shocks, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"shocks must be a dict {{day: fraction}}, got {shocks!r}")
    for day, x in shocks.items():
        if isinstance(day, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(day, (int, np.integer)) \
                or not 0 <= day < days:
            raise ValueError(f"shock day must be a whole number from 0 to {days - 1}, got {day!r}")
        if not _is_number(x) or not x > -1:
            raise ValueError(f"shock on day {day} must be a number above -1 (a fraction), got {x!r}")


def pause_steps(minutes, dt):
    """A pause of `minutes` (of a 390-minute day) in time steps of dt days: at least 1."""
    return max(1, int(round(minutes / MINUTES_PER_DAY / dt)))


def minute_to_step(minute, dt):
    """The time step (counting from 0 at 9:30) that a minute of the day falls in:
    steps 0 .. minute_to_step(c) - 1 are the ones before minute c."""
    return int(round(minute / MINUTES_PER_DAY / dt))


def _is_number(x):
    return isinstance(x, (int, float, np.number)) and not isinstance(x, (bool, np.bool_)) \
        and bool(np.isfinite(x))


def simulate(p, days, seed=None, chartists=True, max_gap=MAX_GAP, max_days=MAX_DAYS,
             breakers=None, shocks=None):
    """Run the market for `days` trading days with settings p.

    Returns a dict of daily series (one value per day's close, days + 1 values):
        lp, lf  log price and log fundamental value (both start at 0)
        z       share of traders who are chartists
        x       chartists' opinion, (optimists - pessimists) / chartists
    plus r, the daily log returns (days values), and halts, the circuit-breaker
    level reached each day (days values: 0 none, 1 or 2 a pause, 3 closed early).
    chartists=False runs the "no chartists" check: everybody is a fundamentalist.
    breakers (check_breakers, e.g. US_BREAKERS) and shocks (check_shocks) are the
    policy options; both off by default, which leaves the model exactly as in SPEC.md.

    Raises RunawayError if the price runs away: more than a factor e^max_gap from
    its value for max_days trading days in a row, or ever more than e^HARD_GAP
    (the paper: no *persistent* pathological mispricing). Bubbles that burst on
    their own are kept. max_gap=None switches the check off.
    """
    check(p)
    if isinstance(days, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(days, (int, np.integer)) or days < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"days must be a whole number >= 1, got {days!r}")
    if not isinstance(chartists, (bool, np.bool_)):
        raise ValueError(f"chartists must be True or False, got {chartists!r}")
    N, floor = int(p["N"]), int(p["floor"])
    each = max(int(N * START_CHARTISTS) // 2, floor) if chartists else 0
    if max_gap is not None and not (isinstance(max_gap, (int, float, np.number))
                                    and not isinstance(max_gap, (bool, np.bool_)) and max_gap > 0):
        raise ValueError(f"max_gap must be a number above 0, or None, got {max_gap!r}")
    if isinstance(max_days, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(max_days, (int, np.integer)) \
            or max_days < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_days must be a whole number >= 1, got {max_days!r}")
    check_breakers(breakers)
    check_shocks(shocks, days)
    if breakers is None:
        cb, halt_steps, pause_end = (-np.inf, -np.inf, -np.inf), 0, 0
    else:
        cb = tuple(float(np.log(1.0 - x)) for x in breakers["levels"])
        halt_steps = pause_steps(breakers["halt_minutes"], p["dt"])
        pause_end = minute_to_step(breakers.get("last_pause_minute", MINUTES_PER_DAY), p["dt"])
    shock = np.zeros(int(days))
    for day, frac in (shocks or {}).items():
        shock[day] += np.log1p(frac)
    lp, lf, z, x, halts, done = _simulate(
        np.random.default_rng(seed), int(days), int(round(1 / p["dt"])), bool(chartists),
        N, *(float(p[k]) for k in ("v1", "v2", "a1", "a2", "a3", "s", "R", "tc", "gamma",
                                   "beta", "sigma_mu", "sigma_eps", "tick")),
        floor, each, each, np.inf if max_gap is None else float(max_gap), int(max_days),
        np.inf if max_gap is None else HARD_GAP, *cb, int(halt_steps), int(pause_end), shock)
    if done < days:
        ratio = np.exp(min(abs(lp[done] - lf[done]), 700.0))   # 700: largest safe exponent
        raise RunawayError(f"day {done}: the price is {ratio:.3g}x away from its value with "
                           f"{z[done]:.0%} chartists and has not come back (a runaway "
                           f"{'bubble' if lp[done] > lf[done] else 'crash'})", done)
    return dict(r=np.diff(lp), lp=lp, lf=lf, z=z, x=x, halts=halts)

"""Measurements of daily returns: fat tails, clustering, predictability.

Each function rejects empty, constant, NaN or infinite input with a clear error.
"""
import numpy as np


def _returns(r):
    """Returns as a 1-D float array; reject empty or NaN/inf input."""
    r = np.asarray(r, dtype=float).ravel()
    if r.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("returns are empty")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(r)):
        raise ValueError("returns contain NaN or infinity")
    return r


def _standardize(r):
    r = _returns(r)
    if r.std() == 0:
        raise ValueError("returns are constant: no spread to measure")
    return (r - r.mean()) / r.std()


def hill_alpha(r, tail=0.05):
    """Hill estimator of the tail exponent of |returns| (top `tail` fraction).

    Zero returns (flat days) are dropped: they carry no tail information.
    Smaller alpha = fatter tail; real markets ~3 (inverse cubic law).
    """
    if not 0 < tail < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"tail must be between 0 and 1, got {tail}")
    a = np.sort(np.abs(_returns(r)))[::-1]
    a = a[a > 0]
    k = max(int(len(a) * tail), 10)
    if len(a) <= k:
        raise ValueError(f"need more than {k} nonzero returns, got {len(a)}")
    if a[0] == a[k]:
        raise ValueError("returns are constant in the tail: no exponent to measure")
    return k / np.sum(np.log(a[:k] / a[k]))


def kurtosis(r):
    """Excess kurtosis: 0 for a bell curve, > 0 for fat tails."""
    return np.mean(_standardize(r) ** 4) - 3


def ccdf(r):
    """Sorted |standardized returns| x and the fraction of days with |z| >= x."""
    z = np.sort(np.abs(_standardize(r)))
    return z, 1 - np.arange(len(z)) / len(z)


def acf(r, lags):
    """Autocorrelation of r at each lag (Pearson correlation of r_t and r_t+lag)."""
    z = _standardize(r)
    lags = np.atleast_1d(lags)
    if lags.size == 0 or not np.all(lags == np.round(lags)):
        raise ValueError(f"lags must be whole numbers, got {lags}")
    lags = lags.astype(int)
    if np.any(lags < 1) or np.any(lags >= len(z) - 1):
        raise ValueError(f"lags must be between 1 and {len(z) - 2}")
    return np.array([np.corrcoef(z[:-k], z[k:])[0, 1] for k in lags])


def aggregate(r, tau):
    """Returns over tau days: sums of tau consecutive daily log returns
    (a leftover partial block at the end is dropped)."""
    r = _returns(r)
    if int(tau) != tau or tau < 1 or tau > len(r):
        raise ValueError(f"tau must be a whole number from 1 to {len(r)}, got {tau}")
    tau = int(tau)
    n = len(r) // tau
    return r[:n * tau].reshape(n, tau).sum(axis=1)


def tail_fit(r, top=0.30):
    """The straight line behind alpha_regression: (alpha, c, x_min, x_max), where the
    share of days with a bigger move is about c * x**-alpha for x_min <= x <= x_max
    (moves in standard deviations; the window is the largest `top` share of days)."""
    if not 0 < top < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"top must be between 0 and 1, got {top}")
    z, cc = ccdf(r)
    k = int(len(z) * (1 - top))
    z, cc = z[k:], cc[k:]
    keep = z > 0
    if keep.sum() < 10 or np.ptp(np.log(z[keep])) == 0:
        raise ValueError("need at least 10 distinct nonzero moves in the fitted window")
    slope, icept = np.polyfit(np.log(z[keep]), np.log(cc[keep]), 1)
    return float(-slope), float(np.exp(icept)), float(z[keep][0]), float(z[-1])


def alpha_regression(r, top=0.30):
    """Tail exponent the way Lux & Marchesi (1999, Fig 2) measure it: the slope of
    log(share of days with a bigger move) against log(move size), fitted over the
    largest `top` share of days. Unlike hill_alpha, this window also covers the
    bell-shaped middle of the distribution, so the two estimates differ."""
    return tail_fit(r, top)[0]


def dfa(x, scales=(16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048)):
    """Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994), as in Lux & Marchesi (1999,
    Fig 3): integrate x, cut it into windows of n days, remove a straight-line trend
    in each, and measure the leftover spread F(n). Returns (scales, F)."""
    x = _returns(x)
    scales = np.asarray(scales, dtype=int)
    if np.any(scales < 4) or np.any(scales > len(x) // 4):
        raise ValueError(f"scales must be between 4 and {len(x) // 4} (a quarter of the data)")
    y = np.cumsum(x - x.mean())
    F = []
    for n in scales:
        seg = y[:len(y) // n * n].reshape(-1, n)
        t = np.arange(n)
        slope, icept = np.polyfit(t, seg.T, 1)
        F.append(np.sqrt(np.mean((seg - (np.outer(slope, t) + icept[:, None])) ** 2)))
    return scales, np.array(F)


def hurst(x, scales=(16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048)):
    """Self-similarity exponent H: the slope of log F(n) against log n from dfa().
    H = 0.5 means no memory; H > 0.5 means memory (persistence); H < 0.5 means
    reversals. Lux & Marchesi (1999): returns 0.48, absolute returns 0.85."""
    s, F = dfa(x, scales)
    return float(np.polyfit(np.log(s), np.log(F), 1)[0])


def dfa_scales(n, smallest=16, count=12):
    """Window sizes for dfa(): `count` sizes spaced evenly on a log scale, from
    `smallest` days up to a quarter of the data (n days)."""
    if n // 4 < smallest:
        raise ValueError(f"need at least {4 * smallest} values for DFA, got {n}")
    return tuple(int(s) for s in np.unique(np.geomspace(smallest, n // 4, count).astype(int)))


FINGERPRINT = {
    "sd": "typical daily move (standard deviation of returns)",
    "kurtosis": "excess kurtosis: 0 for a bell curve, more = fatter tails",
    "alpha_hill": "tail exponent, Hill estimate from the largest 5% of moves (S&P ~3)",
    "alpha_reg": "tail exponent the paper's way: log-log fit to the largest 30% (paper 2.64)",
    "ac_r_1": "correlation of one day's return with the next (about 0 = unpredictable)",
    "ac_abs_1": "correlation of one day's move size with the next (clustering)",
    "ac_abs_50": "the same 50 days apart (long volatility memory)",
    "H": "DFA exponent of returns: 0.5 = no memory (paper 0.48)",
    "H_abs": "DFA exponent of move sizes |r|: above 0.5 = memory (paper 0.85)",
    "kurt_5": "excess kurtosis of 5-day returns",
    "kurt_25": "excess kurtosis of 25-day returns (paper: back to a bell curve)",
}


def fingerprint(r):
    """The numbers that describe a market's returns, as a dict (see FINGERPRINT).
    Needs at least 25 * 20 = 500 days so every measure is defined."""
    r = _returns(r)
    if len(r) < 500:
        raise ValueError(f"need at least 500 days for a fingerprint, got {len(r)}")
    a = np.abs(r)
    scales = dfa_scales(len(r))
    return {
        "sd": float(r.std()),
        "kurtosis": float(kurtosis(r)),
        "alpha_hill": float(hill_alpha(r, 0.05)),
        "alpha_reg": alpha_regression(r),
        "ac_r_1": float(acf(r, 1)[0]),
        "ac_abs_1": float(acf(a, 1)[0]),
        "ac_abs_50": float(acf(a, 50)[0]),
        "H": hurst(r, scales),
        "H_abs": hurst(a, scales),
        "kurt_5": float(kurtosis(aggregate(r, 5))),
        "kurt_25": float(kurtosis(aggregate(r, 25))),
    }

1	"""The Lux-Marchesi (1999) market model, built from the equations in notes/SPEC.md.
2	
3	N traders are in one of three groups:
4	    fundamentalists  buy when the price is below the fundamental value, sell above it
5	    optimists        chartists who buy
6	    pessimists       chartists who sell
7	Traders switch groups at random, at rates that depend on the crowd (herding), the
8	price trend and the profits of each strategy. Excess demand (buyers minus sellers)
9	moves the price one tick at a time. News moves the fundamental value as Gaussian
10	noise, so any fat tails or volatility clustering must come from the traders.
11	
12	Section numbers (sec. 1-5) refer to notes/SPEC.md.
13	
14	Policy options (an extension, not part of the paper; SPEC.md "Policy experiments"):
15	circuit breakers that pause or close trading after a big fall within the day, and
16	one-off policy surprises that move the fundamental value.
17	"""
18	import os
19	
20	import numpy as np
21	
22	try:
23	    import numba
24	except ImportError:                    # still works without numba, just ~50x slower
25	    numba = None
26	
27	# Settings. Every one has a fixed meaning in SPEC.md; rates are per unit of time
28	# (one unit = one trading day).
29	SETTINGS = {
30	    "N": "number of traders",
31	    "v1": "how often chartists reconsider their mood (sec. 1)",
32	    "v2": "how often traders reconsider their strategy (sec. 2)",
33	    "a1": "herding: weight of the majority mood (sec. 1)",
34	    "a2": "trend following: weight of the price trend (sec. 1)",
35	    "a3": "sensitivity to profit differences (sec. 2)",
36	    "s": "discount on fundamentalists' future profits, below 1 (sec. 2)",

79	def check(p):
80	    """Raise ValueError unless p has exactly the known settings with sensible values."""
81	    if not isinstance(p, dict):
82	        raise ValueError(f"settings must be a dict, got {type(p).__name__}")
83	    unknown, missing = set(p) - set(SETTINGS), set(SETTINGS) - set(p)
84	    if unknown or missing:
85	        raise ValueError(f"unknown settings {sorted(unknown)}, missing settings {sorted(missing)}")
86	    for k, v in p.items():
87	        if isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(v, (int, float, np.number)) \
88	                or not np.isfinite(v):
89	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be a finite number, got {v!r}")
90	        if v < 0:
91	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must not be negative, got {v}")
92	    # floor 0 would let the chartists die out: then opinion x = (n+ - n-)/n_c divides by 0
93	    for k in ("N", "v1", "v2", "beta", "tick", "dt", "floor"):
94	        if p[k] <= 0:
95	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be above 0, got {p[k]}")
96	    for k in ("N", "floor"):
97	        if int(p[k]) != p[k]:
98	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be a whole number, got {p[k]}")
99	    if not p["s"] < 1:
100	        raise ValueError(f"s must be below 1 (the paper's discount factor), got {p['s']}")
101	    if not p["tick"] < 1:
102	        raise ValueError(f"tick must be below 1 (a fraction of the price), got {p['tick']}")
103	    steps = round(1 / p["dt"])
104	    if abs(steps * p["dt"] - 1) > 1e-9:
105	        raise ValueError(f"dt must split one day into whole steps (0.01, 0.005, ...), got {p['dt']}")
106	    if TREND_WINDOW / p["dt"] < 1 - 1e-9:
107	        raise ValueError(f"dt must be at most {TREND_WINDOW} (the trend window), got {p['dt']}")
108	    if p["N"] < 4 * p["floor"]:
109	        raise ValueError(f"N={p['N']} is too small for floor={p['floor']}: need N >= 4*floor")

114	def _leave(g, n, rate_a, rate_b, dt):
115	    """Of n traders each leaving at rate_a (to A) or rate_b (to B) per day, how many
116	    go to A and to B within dt. Exact for constant rates: a trader leaves with
117	    probability 1 - exp(-(rate_a + rate_b) dt), then picks A with chance
118	    rate_a / (rate_a + rate_b)."""
119	    total = rate_a + rate_b
120	    if n <= 0 or total <= 0.0:
121	        return 0, 0
122	    k = g.binomial(n, 1.0 - np.exp(-total * dt))
123	    to_a = g.binomial(k, rate_a / total)
124	    return to_a, k - to_a

127	def _cap(u):
128	    return min(U_CAP, max(-U_CAP, u))

131	def _simulate(g, days, steps, chartists, N, v1, v2, a1, a2, a3, s, R, tc, gamma,
132	              beta, sigma_mu, sigma_eps, tick, floor, n_plus, n_minus, max_gap, max_days,
133	              hard_gap, cb1, cb2, cb3, halt_steps, pause_end, shock):
134	    """The simulation loop (see SPEC.md). Returns per-day log price, log value,
135	    chartist share and opinion at each day's close, the circuit-breaker level of
136	    each day, and the number of days completed (fewer than `days` if the price ran
137	    away: |log price - log value| above max_gap for max_days days in a row, or ever
138	    above hard_gap).
139	    Circuit breakers: 0 > cb1 > cb2 > cb3 are log falls from the previous close
140	    (-inf = off). Falling to cb1 or cb2 within the first pause_end steps of the day
141	    freezes the price for halt_steps steps (once each per day; later in the day
142	    nothing happens); falling to cb3 freezes it for the rest of the day, at any time.
143	    Traders keep switching while the price is frozen.
144	    shock[day]: log change of the value at the start of that day (policy surprise)."""
145	    dt = 1.0 / steps
146	    window = int(round(TREND_WINDOW * steps))
147	    up_step, down_step = np.log(1.0 + tick), np.log(1.0 - tick)
148	    # mu is drawn fresh each step; scaled so its effect per day does not depend on
149	    # dt (identical to [S] at their dt = 0.01)
150	    mu_sd = sigma_mu * np.sqrt(REFERENCE_DT / dt)
151	    lp = 0.0                                   # log price; starts at the value
152	    lf = 0.0                                   # log fundamental value
153	    n_f = N - n_plus - n_minus
154	    past = np.zeros(window)                    # log prices of the last `window` steps
155	    out_lp = np.empty(days + 1)
156	    out_lf = np.empty(days + 1)
157	    out_z = np.empty(days + 1)
158	    out_x = np.empty(days + 1)
159	    out_lp[0], out_lf[0] = lp, lf
160	    nc = n_plus + n_minus
161	    out_z[0] = nc / N
162	    out_x[0] = (n_plus - n_minus) / nc if nc > 0 else 0.0
163	    halts = np.zeros(days, dtype=np.int64)     # 0 none, 1-2 pause levels, 3 closed
164	    t = 0
165	    outside = 0                                # days in a row beyond max_gap
166	    for day in range(days):
167	        lf += shock[day]
168	        prev_close = lp
169	        paused = 0                             # steps of pause left
170	        for k in range(steps):
171	            # dp/dt / p: relative price change per day over the trend window
172	            trend = (np.exp(lp - past[t % window]) - 1.0) / TREND_WINDOW
173	            past[t % window] = lp
174	            t += 1
175	            gap = np.exp(lf - lp) - 1.0        # (p_f - p) / p
176	            if chartists:
177	                nc = n_plus + n_minus
178	                # sec. 1: mood. sec. 2: strategy (profit of chartists vs fundamentalists)
179	                U1 = _cap(a1 * (n_plus - n_minus) / nc + a2 / v1 * trend)
180	                gain = R * (1.0 + gap) + trend / v2    # (r + (dp/dt)/v2) / p, r = R p_f
181	                U21 = _cap(a3 * (gain - R - s * abs(gap)))
182	                U22 = _cap(a3 * (R - gain - s * abs(gap)))
183	                mood = v1 * nc / N
184	                # every rate below is per trader per day (first: where they go)
185	                p_to_m, p_to_f = _leave(g, n_plus, mood * np.exp(-U1),
186	                                        v2 * n_f / N * np.exp(-U21), dt)
187	                m_to_p, m_to_f = _leave(g, n_minus, mood * np.exp(U1),
188	                                        v2 * n_f / N * np.exp(-U22), dt)
189	                f_to_p, f_to_m = _leave(g, n_f, v2 * n_plus / N * np.exp(U21),
190	                                        v2 * n_minus / N * np.exp(U22), dt)
191	                # floors (sec. 5): undo just enough moves to keep both groups alive
192	                short_f = floor - (n_f - f_to_p - f_to_m + p_to_f + m_to_f)
193	                while short_f > 0:
194	                    if f_to_p >= f_to_m:
195	                        f_to_p -= 1
196	                    else:
197	                        f_to_m -= 1
198	                    short_f -= 1
199	                short_c = floor - (nc - p_to_f - m_to_f + f_to_p + f_to_m)
200	                while short_c > 0:
201	                    if p_to_f >= m_to_f:
202	                        p_to_f -= 1
203	                    else:
204	                        m_to_f -= 1
205	                    short_c -= 1
206	                n_plus += m_to_p - p_to_m + f_to_p - p_to_f
207	                n_minus += p_to_m - m_to_p + f_to_m - m_to_f
208	                n_f += p_to_f + m_to_f - f_to_p - f_to_m
209	            # sec. 3: excess demand -> random up and down ticks
210	            ed = (n_plus - n_minus) * tc + n_f * gamma * gap
211	            # ticks per day = beta (ED + mu) / tick, so that on average
212	            # d(ln p)/dt = beta (ED + mu), SPEC eq. 25
213	            push = beta * (ed + mu_sd * g.standard_normal()) / tick
214	            if halts[day] == 3 or paused > 0:  # trading halted: the price is frozen
215	                paused = max(0, paused - 1)
216	            else:
217	                if push > 0.0:
218	                    lp += g.poisson(push * dt) * up_step
219	                else:
220	                    lp += g.poisson(-push * dt) * down_step
221	                # circuit breakers: each level fires at most once a day
222	                fall = lp - prev_close
223	                if fall <= cb3:
224	                    halts[day] = 3
225	                elif fall <= cb2 and halts[day] < 2 and k < pause_end:
226	                    halts[day] = 2
227	                    paused = halt_steps
228	                elif fall <= cb1 and halts[day] < 1 and k < pause_end:
229	                    halts[day] = 1
230	                    paused = halt_steps
231	            # sec. 4: news
232	            lf += sigma_eps * np.sqrt(dt) * g.standard_normal()
233	        nc = n_plus + n_minus
234	        out_lp[day + 1], out_lf[day + 1] = lp, lf
235	        out_z[day + 1] = nc / N
236	        out_x[day + 1] = (n_plus - n_minus) / nc if nc > 0 else 0.0
237	        outside = outside + 1 if abs(lp - lf) > max_gap else 0
238	        if outside >= max_days or abs(lp - lf) > hard_gap:
239	            return out_lp, out_lf, out_z, out_x, halts, day + 1
240	    return out_lp, out_lf, out_z, out_x, halts, days

250	def check_breakers(breakers):
251	    """Circuit-breaker rules: dict(levels=(l1, l2, l3), halt_minutes=m), and optionally
252	    last_pause_minute=c. The levels are falls below the previous close (0.07 = 7%),
253	    increasing; l1 and l2 pause trading for m minutes of a 390-minute day, but only
254	    before minute c (no limit if c is left out); l3 closes the day at any time.
255	    None = no breakers."""
256	    if breakers is None:
257	        return
258	    if not isinstance(breakers, dict) or not {"levels", "halt_minutes"} <= set(breakers) \
259	            or not set(breakers) <= {"levels", "halt_minutes", "last_pause_minute"}:
260	        raise ValueError("breakers needs 'levels' and 'halt_minutes' (and optionally "
261	                         f"'last_pause_minute'), got {breakers!r}")
262	    c = breakers.get("last_pause_minute", MINUTES_PER_DAY)
263	    if not _is_number(c) or not 0 <= c <= MINUTES_PER_DAY:
264	        raise ValueError(f"last_pause_minute must be a number from 0 to {MINUTES_PER_DAY}, got {c!r}")
265	    lv = tuple(breakers["levels"])
266	    if len(lv) != 3 or not all(_is_number(x) and 0 < x < 1 for x in lv) \
267	            or not lv[0] < lv[1] < lv[2]:
268	        raise ValueError(f"breaker levels must be 3 increasing falls between 0 and 1, got {lv}")
269	    m = breakers["halt_minutes"]
270	    if not _is_number(m) or not 0 < m <= MINUTES_PER_DAY:
271	        raise ValueError(f"halt_minutes must be a number from 0 to {MINUTES_PER_DAY}, got {m!r}")

274	def check_shocks(shocks, days):
275	    """Policy surprises: {day: fraction}, e.g. {200: -0.1} = at the start of day 200
276	    a surprise cuts the fundamental value by 10%. None = no surprises."""
277	    if shocks is None:
278	        return
279	    if not isinstance(shocks, dict):
280	        raise ValueError(f"shocks must be a dict {{day: fraction}}, got {shocks!r}")
281	    for day, x in shocks.items():
282	        if isinstance(day, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(day, (int, np.integer)) \
283	                or not 0 <= day < days:
284	            raise ValueError(f"shock day must be a whole number from 0 to {days - 1}, got {day!r}")
285	        if not _is_number(x) or not x > -1:
286	            raise ValueError(f"shock on day {day} must be a number above -1 (a fraction), got {x!r}")

289	def pause_steps(minutes, dt):
290	    """A pause of `minutes` (of a 390-minute day) in time steps of dt days: at least 1."""
291	    return max(1, int(round(minutes / MINUTES_PER_DAY / dt)))

294	def minute_to_step(minute, dt):
295	    """The time step (counting from 0 at 9:30) that a minute of the day falls in:
296	    steps 0 .. minute_to_step(c) - 1 are the ones before minute c."""
297	    return int(round(minute / MINUTES_PER_DAY / dt))

300	def _is_number(x):
301	    return isinstance(x, (int, float, np.number)) and not isinstance(x, (bool, np.bool_)) \
302	        and bool(np.isfinite(x))

305	def simulate(p, days, seed=None, chartists=True, max_gap=MAX_GAP, max_days=MAX_DAYS,
306	             breakers=None, shocks=None):
307	    """Run the market for `days` trading days with settings p.
308	
309	    Returns a dict of daily series (one value per day's close, days + 1 values):
310	        lp, lf  log price and log fundamental value (both start at 0)
311	        z       share of traders who are chartists
312	        x       chartists' opinion, (optimists - pessimists) / chartists
313	    plus r, the daily log returns (days values), and halts, the circuit-breaker
314	    level reached each day (days values: 0 none, 1 or 2 a pause, 3 closed early).
315	    chartists=False runs the "no chartists" check: everybody is a fundamentalist.
316	    breakers (check_breakers, e.g. US_BREAKERS) and shocks (check_shocks) are the
317	    policy options; both off by default, which leaves the model exactly as in SPEC.md.
318	
319	    Raises RunawayError if the price runs away: more than a factor e^max_gap from
320	    its value for max_days trading days in a row, or ever more than e^HARD_GAP
321	    (the paper: no *persistent* pathological mispricing). Bubbles that burst on
322	    their own are kept. max_gap=None switches the check off.
323	    """
324	    check(p)
325	    if isinstance(days, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(days, (int, np.integer)) or days < 1:
326	        raise ValueError(f"days must be a whole number >= 1, got {days!r}")
327	    if not isinstance(chartists, (bool, np.bool_)):
328	        raise ValueError(f"chartists must be True or False, got {chartists!r}")
329	    N, floor = int(p["N"]), int(p["floor"])
330	    each = max(int(N * START_CHARTISTS) // 2, floor) if chartists else 0
331	    if max_gap is not None and not (isinstance(max_gap, (int, float, np.number))
332	                                    and not isinstance(max_gap, (bool, np.bool_)) and max_gap > 0):
333	        raise ValueError(f"max_gap must be a number above 0, or None, got {max_gap!r}")
334	    if isinstance(max_days, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(max_days, (int, np.integer)) \
335	            or max_days < 1:
336	        raise ValueError(f"max_days must be a whole number >= 1, got {max_days!r}")
337	    check_breakers(breakers)
338	    check_shocks(shocks, days)
339	    if breakers is None:
340	        cb, halt_steps, pause_end = (-np.inf, -np.inf, -np.inf), 0, 0
341	    else:
342	        cb = tuple(float(np.log(1.0 - x)) for x in breakers["levels"])
343	        halt_steps = pause_steps(breakers["halt_minutes"], p["dt"])
344	        pause_end = minute_to_step(breakers.get("last_pause_minute", MINUTES_PER_DAY), p["dt"])
345	    shock = np.zeros(int(days))
346	    for day, frac in (shocks or {}).items():
347	        shock[day] += np.log1p(frac)
348	    lp, lf, z, x, halts, done = _simulate(
349	        np.random.default_rng(seed), int(days), int(round(1 / p["dt"])), bool(chartists),
350	        N, *(float(p[k]) for k in ("v1", "v2", "a1", "a2", "a3", "s", "R", "tc", "gamma",
351	                                   "beta", "sigma_mu", "sigma_eps", "tick")),
352	        floor, each, each, np.inf if max_gap is None else float(max_gap), int(max_days),
353	        np.inf if max_gap is None else HARD_GAP, *cb, int(halt_steps), int(pause_end), shock)
354	    if done < days:
355	        ratio = np.exp(min(abs(lp[done] - lf[done]), 700.0))   # 700: largest safe exponent
356	        raise RunawayError(f"day {done}: the price is {ratio:.3g}x away from its value with "
357	                           f"{z[done]:.0%} chartists and has not come back (a runaway "
358	                           f"{'bubble' if lp[done] > lf[done] else 'crash'})", done)
359	    return dict(r=np.diff(lp), lp=lp, lf=lf, z=z, x=x, halts=halts)

1	"""Measurements of daily returns: fat tails, clustering, predictability.
2	
3	Each function rejects empty, constant, NaN or infinite input with a clear error.
4	"""
5	import numpy as np
6	
7	
8	def _returns(r):
9	    """Returns as a 1-D float array; reject empty or NaN/inf input."""
10	    r = np.asarray(r, dtype=float).ravel()
11	    if r.size == 0:
12	        raise ValueError("returns are empty")
13	    if not np.all(np.isfinite(r)):
14	        raise ValueError("returns contain NaN or infinity")
15	    return r
16	
17	
18	def _standardize(r):
19	    r = _returns(r)
20	    if r.std() == 0:
21	        raise ValueError("returns are constant: no spread to measure")
22	    return (r - r.mean()) / r.std()
23

25	def hill_alpha(r, tail=0.05):
26	    """Hill estimator of the tail exponent of |returns| (top `tail` fraction).
27	
28	    Zero returns (flat days) are dropped: they carry no tail information.
29	    Smaller alpha = fatter tail; real markets ~3 (inverse cubic law).
30	    """
31	    if not 0 < tail < 1:
32	        raise ValueError(f"tail must be between 0 and 1, got {tail}")
33	    a = np.sort(np.abs(_returns(r)))[::-1]
34	    a = a[a > 0]
35	    k = max(int(len(a) * tail), 10)
36	    if len(a) <= k:
37	        raise ValueError(f"need more than {k} nonzero returns, got {len(a)}")
38	    if a[0] == a[k]:
39	        raise ValueError("returns are constant in the tail: no exponent to measure")
40	    return k / np.sum(np.log(a[:k] / a[k]))
41	
42	
43	def kurtosis(r):
44	    """Excess kurtosis: 0 for a bell curve, > 0 for fat tails."""
45	    return np.mean(_standardize(r) ** 4) - 3
46	
47	
48	def ccdf(r):
49	    """Sorted |standardized returns| x and the fraction of days with |z| >= x."""
50	    z = np.sort(np.abs(_standardize(r)))
51	    return z, 1 - np.arange(len(z)) / len(z)
52

54	def acf(r, lags):
55	    """Autocorrelation of r at each lag (Pearson correlation of r_t and r_t+lag)."""
56	    z = _standardize(r)
57	    lags = np.atleast_1d(lags)
58	    if lags.size == 0 or not np.all(lags == np.round(lags)):
59	        raise ValueError(f"lags must be whole numbers, got {lags}")
60	    lags = lags.astype(int)
61	    if np.any(lags < 1) or np.any(lags >= len(z) - 1):
62	        raise ValueError(f"lags must be between 1 and {len(z) - 2}")
63	    return np.array([np.corrcoef(z[:-k], z[k:])[0, 1] for k in lags])
64	
65	
66	def aggregate(r, tau):
67	    """Returns over tau days: sums of tau consecutive daily log returns
68	    (a leftover partial block at the end is dropped)."""
69	    r = _returns(r)
70	    if int(tau) != tau or tau < 1 or tau > len(r):
71	        raise ValueError(f"tau must be a whole number from 1 to {len(r)}, got {tau}")
72	    tau = int(tau)
73	    n = len(r) // tau
74	    return r[:n * tau].reshape(n, tau).sum(axis=1)

77	def tail_fit(r, top=0.30):
78	    """The straight line behind alpha_regression: (alpha, c, x_min, x_max), where the
79	    share of days with a bigger move is about c * x**-alpha for x_min <= x <= x_max
80	    (moves in standard deviations; the window is the largest `top` share of days)."""
81	    if not 0 < top < 1:
82	        raise ValueError(f"top must be between 0 and 1, got {top}")
83	    z, cc = ccdf(r)
84	    k = int(len(z) * (1 - top))
85	    z, cc = z[k:], cc[k:]
86	    keep = z > 0
87	    if keep.sum() < 10 or np.ptp(np.log(z[keep])) == 0:
88	        raise ValueError("need at least 10 distinct nonzero moves in the fitted window")
89	    slope, icept = np.polyfit(np.log(z[keep]), np.log(cc[keep]), 1)
90	    return float(-slope), float(np.exp(icept)), float(z[keep][0]), float(z[-1])

93	def alpha_regression(r, top=0.30):
94	    """Tail exponent the way Lux & Marchesi (1999, Fig 2) measure it: the slope of
95	    log(share of days with a bigger move) against log(move size), fitted over the
96	    largest `top` share of days. Unlike hill_alpha, this window also covers the
97	    bell-shaped middle of the distribution, so the two estimates differ."""
98	    return tail_fit(r, top)[0]
99	
100	
101	def dfa(x, scales=(16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048)):
102	    """Detrended fluctuation analysis (Peng et al. 1994), as in Lux & Marchesi (1999,
103	    Fig 3): integrate x, cut it into windows of n days, remove a straight-line trend
104	    in each, and measure the leftover spread F(n). Returns (scales, F)."""
105	    x = _returns(x)
106	    scales = np.asarray(scales, dtype=int)
107	    if np.any(scales < 4) or np.any(scales > len(x) // 4):
108	        raise ValueError(f"scales must be between 4 and {len(x) // 4} (a quarter of the data)")
109	    y = np.cumsum(x - x.mean())
110	    F = []
111	    for n in scales:
112	        seg = y[:len(y) // n * n].reshape(-1, n)
113	        t = np.arange(n)
114	        slope, icept = np.polyfit(t, seg.T, 1)
115	        F.append(np.sqrt(np.mean((seg - (np.outer(slope, t) + icept[:, None])) ** 2)))
116	    return scales, np.array(F)
117	
118	
119	def hurst(x, scales=(16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048)):
120	    """Self-similarity exponent H: the slope of log F(n) against log n from dfa().
121	    H = 0.5 means no memory; H > 0.5 means memory (persistence); H < 0.5 means
122	    reversals. Lux & Marchesi (1999): returns 0.48, absolute returns 0.85."""
123	    s, F = dfa(x, scales)
124	    return float(np.polyfit(np.log(s), np.log(F), 1)[0])
125	
126	
127	def dfa_scales(n, smallest=16, count=12):
128	    """Window sizes for dfa(): `count` sizes spaced evenly on a log scale, from
129	    `smallest` days up to a quarter of the data (n days)."""
130	    if n // 4 < smallest:
131	        raise ValueError(f"need at least {4 * smallest} values for DFA, got {n}")
132	    return tuple(int(s) for s in np.unique(np.geomspace(smallest, n // 4, count).astype(int)))
133	
134	
135	FINGERPRINT = {
136	    "sd": "typical daily move (standard deviation of returns)",
137	    "kurtosis": "excess kurtosis: 0 for a bell curve, more = fatter tails",
138	    "alpha_hill": "tail exponent, Hill estimate from the largest 5% of moves (S&P ~3)",
139	    "alpha_reg": "tail exponent the paper's way: log-log fit to the largest 30% (paper 2.64)",
140	    "ac_r_1": "correlation of one day's return with the next (about 0 = unpredictable)",
141	    "ac_abs_1": "correlation of one day's move size with the next (clustering)",
142	    "ac_abs_50": "the same 50 days apart (long volatility memory)",
143	    "H": "DFA exponent of returns: 0.5 = no memory (paper 0.48)",
144	    "H_abs": "DFA exponent of move sizes |r|: above 0.5 = memory (paper 0.85)",
145	    "kurt_5": "excess kurtosis of 5-day returns",
146	    "kurt_25": "excess kurtosis of 25-day returns (paper: back to a bell curve)",
147	}
148	
149	
150	def fingerprint(r):
151	    """The numbers that describe a market's returns, as a dict (see FINGERPRINT).
152	    Needs at least 25 * 20 = 500 days so every measure is defined."""
153	    r = _returns(r)
154	    if len(r) < 500:
155	        raise ValueError(f"need at least 500 days for a fingerprint, got {len(r)}")
156	    a = np.abs(r)
157	    scales = dfa_scales(len(r))
158	    return {
159	        "sd": float(r.std()),
160	        "kurtosis": float(kurtosis(r)),
161	        "alpha_hill": float(hill_alpha(r, 0.05)),
162	        "alpha_reg": alpha_regression(r),
163	        "ac_r_1": float(acf(r, 1)[0]),
164	        "ac_abs_1": float(acf(a, 1)[0]),
165	        "ac_abs_50": float(acf(a, 50)[0]),
166	        "H": hurst(r, scales),
167	        "H_abs": hurst(a, scales),
168	        "kurt_5": float(kurtosis(aggregate(r, 5))),
169	        "kurt_25": float(kurtosis(aggregate(r, 25))),
170	    }

1	"""Fit the model's settings to target numbers (notes/SPEC.md, "Parameters").
2	
3	Two fits, by one method:
4	    paper   reproduce Lux & Marchesi (1999)'s published numbers (alpha 2.64,
5	            H 0.48, H|r| 0.85, back to a bell curve at 25 days, no runaways)
6	    spx     make the model's history look like the S&P 500's (its fingerprint)
7	
8	Method: (1) score random settings drawn from RANGES; (2) refine the best few with
9	Nelder-Mead; (3) stability screen: run each refined candidate for STABILITY_DAYS on
10	STABILITY_SEEDS and keep the best-scoring one among those that never run away
11	(a runaway can be too rare to show up in the shorter fitting runs). Every score
12	uses the same TRAIN_SEEDS (so two settings are compared on the same luck); checks
13	of a fitted model must use other seeds (HELD_OUT_SEEDS).
14	
15	Run:  python3 -m herding.calibrate paper      -> settings/paper.json
16	      python3 -m herding.calibrate spx        -> settings/spx.json
17	      add --refine to polish the saved settings on all 8 training seeds
18	      add --draws N to score N random settings in step 1 (default 1200)
19	"""
20	import json
21	import sys
22	import time
23	from multiprocessing import Pool
24	from pathlib import Path
25	
26	import numpy as np
27	
28	from . import market_data, model, stats
29	
30	SETTINGS_DIR = market_data.ROOT / "settings"
31	BURN = 1000                       # days dropped at the start, so the start does not matter
32	TRAIN_SEEDS = tuple(range(100, 108))
33	HELD_OUT_SEEDS = tuple(range(1000, 1040))
34	STABILITY_SEEDS = tuple(range(2000, 2020))   # the stability screen: neither training nor held out
35	STABILITY_DAYS = 100_000                     # about 400 years of trading days per history
36	
37	# Settings that are fitted, with search ranges (low, high, "log" or "lin").
38	RANGES = {
39	    "v1": (0.2, 5.0, "log"), "v2": (0.2, 5.0, "log"),
40	    "a1": (0.0, 1.2, "lin"), "a2": (0.0, 2.0, "lin"), "a3": (0.1, 3.0, "log"),
41	    "tc": (5e-4, 0.05, "log"), "gamma": (2e-3, 0.05, "log"), "beta": (1.0, 20.0, "log"),
42	    "sigma_mu": (0.0, 0.1, "lin"),
43	}
44	SPX_RANGES = dict(RANGES, sigma_eps=(0.002, 0.02, "log"))   # the S&P also sets the scale
45	# Settings that stay at parameter set I: N=500, s=0.75, R=0.0004, tick=0.001,
46	# dt=0.01, floor=4 (and sigma_eps=0.005 in the paper fit).
47	
48	# Paper fit: (value, tolerance) for each published number, and the longest
49	# aggregated kurtosis allowed (the paper: a cross-over to the normal distribution).
50	# The tolerances are this project's own yardsticks, NOT the paper's error bars.
51	# The paper's bars (from its Fig 2 and 3 captions: alpha 0.077, H 0.003, H|r| 0.010)
52	# are regression errors from one long run; they are smaller than how much these numbers change from
53	# one run of the model to the next (H of |returns| varies by about 0.02), so no
54	# setting could match them on every seed. The wider tolerances allow for that.
55	PAPER_TARGETS = {"alpha_reg": (2.64, 0.15), "H": (0.48, 0.03), "H_abs": (0.85, 0.03)}
56	PAPER_KURT_25_MAX = 1.0
57	PAPER_DAYS = 50_000
58	# S&P fit: every fingerprint measure. The tolerance of each is how uncertain the
59	# S&P's own value is: its spread when the S&P's history is resampled in one-year
60	# blocks (a block bootstrap). It does not depend on the model, so a model cannot
61	# look "typical" just by being wildly variable (the first version of this fit,
62	# which divided by the model's own spread, did exactly that).
63	SPX_TARGETS = tuple(stats.FINGERPRINT)
64	BOOTSTRAP_BLOCK, BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS = 250, 200
65	SPX_MAX_DAYS = 1
66	RUNAWAY_LOSS = 1e4
67	
68	
69	def base():
70	    return dict(model.SET_I)
71	
72	
73	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ settings <-> numbers
74	
75	def to_vector(p, ranges):
76	    """Settings as optimizer coordinates: log for "log" settings, as-is for "lin"."""
77	    return np.array([np.log(p[k]) if kind == "log" else p[k]
78	                     for k, (_, _, kind) in ranges.items()])
79	
80	
81	def from_vector(v, ranges, start=None):
82	    """Inverse of to_vector; values outside the ranges are clipped back in."""
83	    p = dict(base() if start is None else start)
84	    for x, (k, (lo, hi, kind)) in zip(v, ranges.items()):
85	        x = float(np.exp(x)) if kind == "log" else float(x)
86	        p[k] = min(hi, max(lo, x))
87	    return p
88	
89	
90	def draw(rng, ranges, start=None):
91	    """Random settings, uniform within each range (on a log scale for "log")."""
92	    p = dict(base() if start is None else start)
93	    for k, (lo, hi, kind) in ranges.items():
94	        p[k] = float(np.exp(rng.uniform(np.log(lo), np.log(hi)))) if kind == "log" \
95	            else float(rng.uniform(lo, hi))
96	    return p
97	
98	
99	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ measuring
100	
101	def histories(p, seeds, days, max_days=model.MAX_DAYS):
102	    """Daily returns of one history per seed (after BURN days), or None if any runs
103	    away (max_days=1: any day more than 2.7x from the value counts as a runaway)."""
104	    out = []
105	    for s in seeds:
106	        try:
107	            out.append(model.simulate(p, days + BURN, seed=s, max_days=max_days)["r"][BURN:])
108	        except model.RunawayError:
109	            return None
110	    return out
111	
112	
113	def ensemble(p, seeds, days, max_days=model.MAX_DAYS):
114	    """Fingerprints of one history per seed, as {measure: array}, or None on a runaway."""
115	    runs = histories(p, seeds, days, max_days)
116	    if runs is None:
117	        return None
118	    rows = [stats.fingerprint(r) for r in runs]
119	    return {k: np.array([f[k] for f in rows]) for k in stats.FINGERPRINT}
120	
121	
122	def paper_loss(fp):
123	    """How far a model is from the paper's numbers, in units of their tolerances."""
124	    if fp is None:
125	        return RUNAWAY_LOSS
126	    loss = sum(((np.mean(fp[k]) - v) / tol) ** 2 for k, (v, tol) in PAPER_TARGETS.items())
127	    return float(loss + max(0.0, np.mean(fp["kurt_25"]) - PAPER_KURT_25_MAX) ** 2)
128	
129	
130	def block_bootstrap(r, block=BOOTSTRAP_BLOCK, draws=BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS, seed=0):
131	    """Fingerprints of `draws` resampled histories, each built from random blocks of
132	    `block` consecutive days (wrapping around), so day-to-day clustering survives."""
133	    r = np.asarray(r, dtype=float)
134	    n = len(r)
135	    if not 1 <= block <= n:
136	        raise ValueError(f"block must be between 1 and {n}, got {block}")
137	    g = np.random.default_rng(seed)
138	    out = []
139	    for _ in range(draws):
140	        starts = g.integers(0, n, -(-n // block))
141	        idx = ((starts[:, None] + np.arange(block)[None, :]).ravel()[:n]) % n
142	        out.append(stats.fingerprint(r[idx]))
143	    return out
144	
145	
146	def spx_tolerance(r):
147	    """How uncertain each S&P fingerprint measure is (block-bootstrap spread)."""
148	    rows = block_bootstrap(r)
149	    return {k: float(np.std([f[k] for f in rows])) for k in SPX_TARGETS}
150	
151	
152	def spx_loss(fp, target, tol):
153	    """Mean squared gap between the model's median and the S&P, each gap in units of
154	    the S&P's own uncertainty (tol). About 1 or less = within the S&P's own noise."""
155	    if fp is None:
156	        return RUNAWAY_LOSS
157	    gaps = [(np.median(fp[k]) - target[k]) / tol[k] for k in SPX_TARGETS]
158	    return float(np.mean(np.square(gaps)))
159	
160	
161	def spx_target():
162	    return stats.fingerprint(market_data.spx_returns().values)
163	
164	
165	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ one fit
166	
167	def fit_seeds(kind):
168	    """The seeds a fit scores every candidate on (the paper fit uses long runs, so 2)."""
169	    return TRAIN_SEEDS[:2] if kind == "paper" else TRAIN_SEEDS
170	
171	
172	class Fit:
173	    """Everything a fit needs, in one picklable object (for multiprocessing)."""
174	
175	    def __init__(self, kind):
176	        if kind not in ("paper", "spx"):
177	            raise ValueError(f"kind must be 'paper' or 'spx', got {kind!r}")
178	        self.kind = kind
179	        self.ranges = RANGES if kind == "paper" else SPX_RANGES
180	        # The S&P never sat 2.7x away from its value, even for a day, so the S&P fit
181	        # rejects any such bubble; the paper fit only rejects persistent ones, as
182	        # the paper says ("no persistent deviations").
183	        self.max_days = SPX_MAX_DAYS if kind == "spx" else model.MAX_DAYS
184	        if kind == "paper":
185	            self.days, self.seeds, self.target = PAPER_DAYS, fit_seeds(kind), None
186	        else:
187	            self.target = spx_target()
188	            self.tol = spx_tolerance(market_data.spx_returns().values)
189	            self.days, self.seeds = len(market_data.spx_returns()), fit_seeds(kind)
190	
191	    def loss(self, p):
192	        fp = ensemble(p, self.seeds, self.days, self.max_days)
193	        return paper_loss(fp) if self.kind == "paper" else spx_loss(fp, self.target, self.tol)
194	
195	    def score_draw(self, i):
196	        p = draw(np.random.default_rng(10_000 + i), self.ranges)
197	        return self.loss(p), p
198	
199	    def loss_of_vector(self, v):
200	        return self.loss(from_vector(v, self.ranges))
201	
202	
203	class SavedLoss:
204	    """A loss function whose every score is saved as one JSON line in `path`. A
205	    score already in the file is read back instead of recomputed. Nelder-Mead is
206	    deterministic, so a refinement restarted after a stop asks for the same points
207	    in the same order and replays the saved ones instantly."""
208	
209	    def __init__(self, fn, path):
210	        self.fn, self.path, self.cache = fn, Path(path), {}
211	        if self.path.exists():
212	            for line in self.path.read_text().splitlines():
213	                try:
214	                    rec = json.loads(line)
215	                except json.JSONDecodeError:          # a line cut off mid-write
216	                    continue
217	                self.cache[tuple(rec["v"])] = rec["loss"]
218	
219	    def __call__(self, v):
220	        key = tuple(float(x) for x in v)
221	        if key not in self.cache:
222	            self.cache[key] = float(self.fn(np.array(key)))
223	            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
224	            with self.path.open("a") as f:
225	                if f.tell() and not self.path.read_bytes().endswith(b"\n"):
226	                    f.write("\n")
227	                f.write(json.dumps({"v": list(key), "loss": self.cache[key]}) + "\n")
228	        return self.cache[key]
229	
230	
231	def _refine(args):
232	    from scipy.optimize import minimize   # here, not on top: only fits need slow-to-load scipy
233	    fit, p, iters = args[:3]
234	    loss = fit.loss_of_vector if len(args) < 4 else SavedLoss(fit.loss_of_vector, args[3])
235	    res = minimize(loss, to_vector(p, fit.ranges), method="Nelder-Mead",
236	                   options=dict(maxfev=iters, xatol=1e-3, fatol=1e-3))
237	    return float(res.fun), from_vector(res.x, fit.ranges)
238	
239	
240	def _runs_away(args):
241	    p, seed, days = args
242	    try:
243	        model.simulate(p, days, seed=seed)
244	    except model.RunawayError:
245	        return True
246	    return False
247	
248	
249	def runaways(pool, p, seeds=STABILITY_SEEDS, days=STABILITY_DAYS):
250	    """How many of the long histories (one per seed) run away, by the model's own
251	    rule (more than e away from the value for MAX_DAYS days in a row)."""
252	    return int(sum(pool.map(_runs_away, [(p, int(s), int(days)) for s in seeds])))
253	
254	
255	def screen(pool, candidates, seeds=STABILITY_SEEDS, days=STABILITY_DAYS):
256	    """Stability screen: sort (loss, settings) candidates by (runaways, loss), so the
257	    best fit among the never-runaway ones comes first. Returns (runaways, loss, p)."""
258	    # one pool.map over every (candidate, seed), so no worker waits between candidates
259	    jobs = [(p, int(s), int(days)) for _, p in candidates for s in seeds]
260	    ran_away = pool.map(_runs_away, jobs, chunksize=1)
261	    counts = [int(sum(ran_away[i * len(seeds):(i + 1) * len(seeds)])) for i in range(len(candidates))]
262	    out = sorted(((bad, loss, p) for bad, (loss, p) in zip(counts, candidates)),
263	                 key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1]))
264	    for bad, loss, _ in out:
265	        print(f"  candidate loss {loss:.3f}: {bad} of {len(seeds)} long histories ran away")
266	    return out
267	
268	
269	CHECKPOINT_DIR = market_data.ROOT / "scratch" / "calibrate"   # git-ignored
270	
271	
272	def checkpointed(pool, fn, jobs, path):
273	    """pool.map(fn, jobs), but each result is saved as one JSON line in `path` as
274	    soon as it is done, and results already in the file are not recomputed. So a
275	    fit that is stopped (a flat battery) loses at most the jobs that were running.
276	    Every result must be JSON-friendly; lists come back as tuples."""
277	    path = Path(path)
278	    done = {}
279	    if path.exists():
280	        for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
281	            try:
282	                rec = json.loads(line)
283	            except json.JSONDecodeError:              # a line cut off mid-write
284	                continue
285	            done[rec["i"]] = tuple(rec["out"]) if isinstance(rec["out"], list) else rec["out"]
286	    todo = [i for i in range(len(jobs)) if i not in done]
287	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
288	    with path.open("a") as f:
289	        if path.stat().st_size and not path.read_bytes().endswith(b"\n"):
290	            f.write("\n")                            # end a line cut off mid-write
291	        for i, out in zip(todo, pool.imap(fn, [jobs[i] for i in todo])):
292	            f.write(json.dumps({"i": i, "out": out}) + "\n")
293	            f.flush()
294	            done[i] = tuple(out) if isinstance(out, list) else out
295	    return [done[i] for i in range(len(jobs))]
296	
297	
298	def run(kind, draws=1200, keep=8, iters=150, workers=8, checkpoint_dir=CHECKPOINT_DIR):
299	    """Random search, Nelder-Mead from the `keep` best, then the stability screen;
300	    returns (loss, settings, runaways). Progress is saved in checkpoint_dir, so
301	    running the same command again after a stop continues where it was; the
302	    checkpoint files are removed once the fit has finished."""
303	    fit = Fit(kind)
304	    t = time.time()
305	    tag = Path(checkpoint_dir) / f"{kind}_draws{draws}_keep{keep}_iters{iters}"
306	    with Pool(workers) as pool:
307	        scored = checkpointed(pool, fit.score_draw, list(range(draws)), f"{tag}_search.jsonl")
308	        scored.sort(key=lambda d: d[0])
309	        print(f"{kind}: {draws} random settings in {time.time() - t:.0f}s; "
310	              f"best loss {scored[0][0]:.2f}; runaways {sum(s >= RUNAWAY_LOSS for s, _ in scored)}",
311	              flush=True)
312	        refined = checkpointed(pool, _refine, [(fit, p, iters, f"{tag}_refine{j}_scores.jsonl")
313	                                               for j, (_, p) in enumerate(scored[:keep])],
314	                               f"{tag}_refine.jsonl")
315	        print(f"{kind}: refined {keep} in {time.time() - t:.0f}s total; stability screen:", flush=True)
316	        bad, loss, p = screen(pool, refined)[0]
317	    print(f"{kind}: chose loss {loss:.3f} ({bad} runaways) after {time.time() - t:.0f}s")
318	    for part in ["search", "refine"] + [f"refine{j}_scores" for j in range(keep)]:
319	        Path(f"{tag}_{part}.jsonl").unlink(missing_ok=True)
320	    return loss, p, bad
321	
322	
323	class _PoolFit(Fit):
324	    """A Fit that runs its seeds in parallel (for refining one candidate at a time)."""
325	
326	    def __init__(self, kind, pool, seeds):
327	        super().__init__(kind)
328	        self.pool, self.seeds = pool, tuple(seeds)
329	
330	    def loss(self, p):
331	        rows = self.pool.map(_fingerprint_one, [(p, s, self.days, self.max_days) for s in self.seeds])
332	        fp = None if any(r is None for r in rows) else \
333	            {k: np.array([r[k] for r in rows]) for k in stats.FINGERPRINT}
334	        return paper_loss(fp) if self.kind == "paper" else spx_loss(fp, self.target, self.tol)
335	
336	
337	def _fingerprint_one(args):
338	    p, seed, days, max_days = args
339	    runs = histories(p, (seed,), days, max_days)
340	    return None if runs is None else stats.fingerprint(runs[0])
341	
342	
343	def refine_saved(kind, iters=200, workers=8):
344	    """Nelder-Mead from the saved settings, scoring every candidate on all
345	    TRAIN_SEEDS (the first fit may use fewer, which can overfit to lucky seeds).
346	    The refined settings replace the saved ones only if they pass the stability
347	    screen at least as well. Returns (loss, settings, runaways)."""
348	    from scipy.optimize import minimize
349	    start = load(kind)
350	    with Pool(workers) as pool:
351	        fit = _PoolFit(kind, pool, TRAIN_SEEDS)
352	        first = fit.loss(start)
353	        res = minimize(fit.loss_of_vector, to_vector(start, fit.ranges), method="Nelder-Mead",
354	                       options=dict(maxfev=iters, xatol=1e-3, fatol=1e-3))
355	        print(f"{kind}: loss on all {len(TRAIN_SEEDS)} training seeds {first:.3f} -> {res.fun:.3f}; "
356	              "stability screen:", flush=True)
357	        bad, loss, p = screen(pool, [(float(res.fun), from_vector(res.x, fit.ranges)),
358	                                     (float(first), start)])[0]
359	    return loss, p, bad
360	
361	
362	def save(kind, loss, p, seeds=None, runaways=None, draws=None):
363	    SETTINGS_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
364	    seeds = fit_seeds(kind) if seeds is None else seeds
365	    out = dict(kind=kind, loss=loss, train_seeds=list(seeds), burn=BURN,
366	               fitted=list(SPX_RANGES if kind == "spx" else RANGES), settings=p)
367	    if draws is not None:
